**Course source:** Day 1 §4.1–§4.2. **Running system:** Order, Product, and User services.

## The registry is now critical infrastructure

If Order can contact only one Eureka server, a registry failure may prevent new lookups, registration or recovery. The course extends Eureka to a cluster and discusses delayed registration, instance eviction and displaying IP addresses.

A typical high-availability configuration uses multiple Eureka servers that replicate registration information. Clients are configured with more than one registry endpoint so that a single server failure is not an immediate control-plane outage.

~~~text
          Eureka A <----peer data----> Eureka B
            ^   ^                        ^   ^
            |   +---- Product A          |   +---- Product B
            +-------- Order -----------+
~~~

## Separate discovery availability from business availability

An existing client may retain a cached instance list when the registry is unavailable. This can keep some requests flowing, but the cached list may become stale. New instances might be invisible until discovery is restored.

A common mistake is to measure only registry health. Instead track registration age, lease renewals, successful discovery lookups and the rate of calls to unavailable instances.

## Operational questions

**Slow registration:** check when the client sends registration, when servers incorporate it and when consumers refresh their cache. These are three different events.

**Slow eviction:** a crashed Product node can appear healthy for a while. A request timeout or connection failure remains possible even after correct discovery.

**Wrong IP address:** the service may publish an interface unreachable from consumers. Verify advertised addresses across containers, hosts and network namespaces.

## Deliberate trade-off

Shorter leases reduce stale entries but increase sensitivity to temporary network disruption. Longer leases tolerate short interruptions but delay eviction. Tune from observed failure behaviour, not from a universal magic number.

## Test your reasoning

Name the component that owns this responsibility, explain its behaviour during a failure, and identify one configuration or metric you would verify in production.

## Mathematical Abstraction

Registry replication may yield temporarily divergent membership views.

$$
D_t^{(A)}(s)\neq D_t^{(B)}(s)
$$

$A$ and $B$ identify two registry replicas. The inequality is possible during propagation delays; it does not assert permanent inconsistency.
